value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 時望氣者言廣陵有天子氣，故封為廣陵王，邑五萬戶。
value.en: Astrologers said Guangling bore an emperor's aura, so Yu was made Prince of Guangling with fifty thousand households.
value.literal: At the time, observers of celestial portents said Guangling had the aura of a Son of Heaven; therefore he was enfeoffed as Prince of Guangling with a fief of fifty thousand households.

value.zh: 以劉寔為師，孟珩為友，楊准、馮蓀為文學。
value.en: Liu Shi served as tutor, Meng Heng as companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun as literary aides.
value.literal: Liu Shi was made tutor, Meng Heng companion, and Yang Zhun and Feng Sun literary aides.

value.zh: 惠帝即位，立為皇太子。
value.en: When Hui Di took the throne, Yu was made crown prince.
value.literal: When Emperor Hui succeeded to the throne, he was established as crown prince.

value.zh: 盛選德望以為師傅，以何劭為太師，王戎為太傅，楊濟為太保，裴楷為少師，張華為少傅，和嶠為少保。
value.en: The court recruited eminent tutors—He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.
value.literal: Worthy men of virtue and repute were abundantly selected as tutors and guardians: He Shao as Grand Tutor, Wang Rong as Grand Mentor, Yang Ji as Grand Guardian, Pei Kai as Junior Tutor, Zhang Hua as Junior Mentor, and He Qiao as Junior Guardian.

value.zh: 元康元年，出就東宮，又詔曰：「遹尚幼蒙，今出東宮，惟當賴師傅群賢之訓。
value.en: In Yuankang year one he moved to the Eastern Palace, and an edict declared: "Yu is still young and inexperienced; now that he has moved to the Eastern Palace he must rely on his tutors and worthy mentors for instruction.
value.literal: In the first year of Yuankang he moved out to the Eastern Palace; an edict further said: "Yu is still young and untutored; now that he is moving out to the Eastern Palace he should rely solely on the instruction of his tutors and the worthy assembly.

value.zh: 其遊處左右，宜得正人使共周旋，能相長益者。」
value.en: Those about him in leisure and attendance should be upright men who keep company with him and help one another improve."
value.literal: Those who attend him in leisure and service should be upright men who may keep company with him and mutually aid one another's growth."

value.zh: 於是使太保衛瓘息庭、司空泰息略、太子太傅楊濟息毖、太子少師裴楷息憲、太子少傅張華息禕、尚書令華暠息恆與太子游處，以相輔導焉。
value.en: Thereupon Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Yang Ji's son Bi, Pei Kai's son Xian, Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Hua Gao's son Heng were sent to keep company with the crown prince and guide him.
value.literal: Thereupon Grand Guardian Wei Guan's son Ting, Director of Works Tai's son Lue, Grand Mentor to the Crown Prince Yang Ji's son Bi, Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince Pei Kai's son Xian, Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince Zhang Hua's son Yi, and Minister Director Hua Gao's son Heng were assigned to keep company with the crown prince and assist in his guidance.

value.zh: 太祖武皇帝，諱克用，本姓朱耶氏，其先隴右金城人也。
value.en: The Supreme Ancestor Martial Emperor, personal name Keyong, was born of the Zhuye clan; his ancestors came from Jincheng in Longyou.
value.literal: Supreme Ancestor Martial Emperor, taboo name Keyong, originally surnamed Zhuye; his forebears were men of Jincheng in Longyou.

value.zh: 始祖拔野，唐貞觀中為墨離軍使，從太宗討高麗、薛延陁有功，為金方道副都護，因家於瓜州。
value.en: The founding ancestor Baye served as Mori Army commissioner under Zhenguan; he followed Taizong against Goguryeo and the Xueyantuo, was rewarded as deputy protector of the Jin-fang Circuit, and settled his family at Guazhou.
value.literal: Founding ancestor Baye, in Tang Zhenguan served as Mori Army commissioner; following Taizong in campaigns against Goguryeo and the Xueyantuo he had merit, was made Deputy Protector-General of the Jin-fang Circuit, and took residence at Guazhou.

value.zh: 太宗平薛延陁諸部，於安西、北庭置都護屬之，分同羅、仆骨之人，置沙陁都督府。
value.en: After Taizong subdued the Xueyantuo, he set protectors at Anxi and Beiting, assigned the Tongluo and Pugu to them, and founded the Shatuo Chief Commandery.
value.literal: Taizong pacified the Xueyantuo tribes, placed protectors at Anxi and Beiting subject to them, divided the Tongluo and Pugu peoples, and established the Shatuo Chief Commandery.

value.zh: 蓋北庭有磧曰沙陁，故因以為名焉。
value.en: A desert tract at Beiting was called Shatuo, and the name followed from that.
value.literal: For Beiting had a desert tract called Shatuo, hence the name.

value.zh: 永徽中，以拔野為都督，其後子孫五世相承。
value.en: Under Yonghui, Baye became chief; five generations of his line succeeded one another.
value.literal: In Yonghui, Baye was made chief; thereafter descendants held the post for five generations in succession.

value.zh: 曾祖盡忠，貞元中，繼為沙陀府都督。
value.en: His great-grandfather Jingzhong became Shatuo prefectural chief in the Zhenyuan era.
value.literal: Great-grandfather Jingzhong, in Zhenyuan, succeeded as Shatuo prefectural chief.

value.zh: 既而為吐蕃所陷，乃舉其族七千帳徙於甘州。
value.en: The Tibetans soon overran him; he led seven thousand tents of his clan to relocate at Ganzhou.
value.literal: Soon after he was trapped by the Tibetans; he then moved his clan, seven thousand tents, to Ganzhou.

value.zh: 盡忠尋率部眾三萬東奔，俄而吐蕃追兵大至，盡忠戰歿。
value.en: Jingzhong soon fled east with thirty thousand followers; Tibetan pursuit caught up and he fell in battle.
value.literal: Jingzhong soon led thirty thousand of his following east in flight; presently Tibetan pursuers came in force and Jingzhong died in battle.

value.zh: 祖執宜，即盡忠之長子也，收合餘眾，至於靈州，德宗命為陰山府都督。
value.en: His grandfather Zhiyi, Jingzhong's eldest son, rallied the survivors, reached Lingzhou, and Dezong made him governor of Yinshan Prefecture.
value.literal: Grandfather Zhiyi, Jingzhong's eldest son, gathered the remnant following, reached Lingzhou, and Dezong appointed him governor of Yinshan Prefecture.

value.zh: 元和初，入為金吾將軍，遷蔚州刺史、代北行營招撫使。
value.en: Early in Yuanhe he became a Golden Crow general, then prefect of Wei and pacification commissioner for the northern Dai frontier.
value.literal: At the start of Yuanhe he entered court as Golden Crow general, was transferred to prefect of Wei, and northern campaign pacification commissioner for Dai.

value.zh: 〈（《新唐書·沙陀傳》：元和三年，盡忠款靈州塞，詔處其部鹽州置陰山府，以執宜為府兵馬使。
value.en: (The 《New Tang History · Shatuo Treatise》 says: In Yuanhe 3 Jingzhong came in at Lingzhou; the court settled his people at Yanzhou as Yinshan Prefecture and made Zhiyi its horse commissioner.
value.literal: (The 《New Tang History · Shatuo Treatise》: In Yuanhe year 3 Jingzhong submitted at the Lingzhou pass; an edict settled his tribe at Yanzhou and established Yinshan Prefecture, making Zhiyi prefectural horse commissioner.

value.zh: 朝長安，授特進、金吾衛將軍。
value.en: At Chang'an he received Special Advancement and a post in the Golden Crow Guard.
value.literal: He attended court at Chang'an and was given Special Advancement and general of the Golden Crow Guard.

value.zh: 從攻鎮州，進蔚州刺史。
value.en: He took part in the Zhenzhou campaign and was promoted to Wei prefect.
value.literal: Following the attack on Zhen prefecture, he was advanced to prefect of Wei.

value.zh: 破吳元濟，授檢校刑部尚書。
value.en: After Wu Yuanji was broken he received the acting post of Minister of Justice.
value.literal: Defeating Wu Yuanji, he was made acting Minister of Justice.

value.zh: 長慶初，破賊深州，入朝留宿衛，拜金吾衛將軍。
value.en: Early in Changqing he crushed rebels at Shenzhou, stayed at court on palace guard duty, and became a Golden Crow Guard general.
value.literal: At the start of Changqing he defeated bandits at Shen prefecture, entered court and remained on palace guard, and was made general of the Golden Crow Guard.

value.zh: 太和中，授陰山府都督、代北行營招撫使。）〉
value.en: Under Taihe he was named governor of Yinshan Prefecture and northern campaign pacification commissioner for Dai.)〉
value.literal: In Taihe he was given Yinshan Prefecture governorship and northern campaign pacification commissioner for Dai.)〉

value.zh: 莊宗即位，追諡為昭烈皇帝，廟號懿祖。
value.en: Zhuangzong enthroned him posthumously as Emperor Zhaolie with temple name Ancestor Yi.
value.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne he was posthumously honored as Emperor Zhaolie, temple name Ancestor Yi.

value.zh: 烈考國昌，本名赤心，唐朔州刺史。
value.en: His father Guochang, born Chixin, had been Tang prefect of Shuo.
value.literal: His stern father Guochang, original name Chixin, was Tang prefect of Shuo.

value.zh: 咸通中，討龐勳有功，入為金吾上將軍，賜姓李氏，名國昌，
value.en: Under Xiantong he helped crush Pang Xun, entered court as supreme Golden Crow general, and received the imperial surname Li and the name Guochang,
value.literal: In Xiantong, campaigning against Pang Xun with merit, he entered court as supreme Golden Crow general, was granted the surname Li and the name Guochang,

value.zh: 〈（代州有《唐故龍武軍統軍檢校司徒贈太保隴四李公神道碑》云：公諱國昌，字德興。）〉
value.en: (A Dai stele, the 《Stele of Lord Li, Late Tang Longwu Commander, Acting Minister of Works, Posthumously Grand Guardian of Longxi》, records: the lord's taboo name was Guochang, style Dexing.)〉
value.literal: (At Dai prefecture there is the 《Stele of the Late Tang Longwu Army Commander-in-Chief, Acting Minister of Works, Posthumously Grand Guardian of Longxi, Lord Li》 saying: the lord's taboo name was Guochang, style Dexing.)〉

value.zh: 仍係鄭王房。
value.en: and he was entered in the genealogical line of the Prince of Zheng.
value.literal: and he was enrolled in the Prince of Zheng branch.

value.zh: 出為振武節度使，尋為吐渾所襲，退保於神武川。
value.en: He was posted as Zhenwu military commissioner; the Tuyuhun soon struck, and he fell back to Shenwu River.
value.literal: He went out as Zhenwu military commissioner; soon the Tuyuhun attacked and he withdrew to hold Shenwu River.

value.zh: 及武皇鎮太原，表為代北軍節度使。
value.en: When Wuhuang held Taiyuan he memorialized Guochang as military commissioner of the northern Dai army.
value.literal: When Wuhuang held Taiyuan he memorialized him as northern-campaign military commissioner.

value.zh: 中和三年薨。
value.en: He died in Zhonghe 3.
value.literal: He died in the third year of Zhonghe.

value.zh: 莊宗即位，追諡為文皇，廟號獻祖。
value.en: Zhuangzong enthroned him posthumously as Emperor Wen with temple name Ancestor Xian.
value.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne he was posthumously honored as Emperor Wen, temple name Ancestor Xian.

value.zh: 三月，邢州節度使安知建叛，奔青州。
value.en: In the third month Xing military commissioner An Zhijian rebelled and fled to Qingzhou.
value.literal: In the third month Xing military commissioner An Zhijian rebelled and fled to Qingzhou.

value.zh: 天子以知建為神武統軍，自棣州溯河歸朝。
value.en: The emperor named him commander of the Divine Martial Army and ordered him to return to court up the river from Di Prefecture.
value.literal: The Son of Heaven made Zhijian commander of the Divine Martial Army and ordered him to return to court by river upstream from Di Prefecture.

value.zh: 鄆州朱瑄邀斬於河上，傳首晉陽。
value.en: Zhu Xuan of Yanzhou cut him down on the river and sent his head to Jinyang.
value.literal: Yanzhou's Zhu Xuan intercepted and beheaded him on the river, and sent the head to Jinyang.

value.zh: 以李存孝為邢州節度使。
value.en: Li Cunxiao was made military commissioner of Xing.
value.literal: Li Cunxiao was made military commissioner of Xing.

value.zh: 四月，武皇大舉兵討赫連鐸於雲州，遣騎將薛阿檀率前軍以進攻，武皇設伏兵於御河之上，大破之，因塹守其城。
value.en: In the fourth month Wuhuang raised a great army against Helian Duo at Yunzhou, sent the cavalry commander Xue Atan with the vanguard to press the attack, and set ambushers along the Yu River; he broke Duo utterly and then walled the city in.
value.literal: In the fourth month Wuhuang raised a great army to attack Helian Duo at Yun Prefecture, sent cavalry commander Xue Atan with the vanguard to advance the assault; Wuhuang set ambush troops above the Yu River, routed them utterly, and thereby besieged the city with trenches.

value.zh: 七月，武皇進軍柳會，赫連鐸力屈食盡，奔於吐渾部，遂歸幽州，雲州平。
value.en: In the seventh month Wuhuang advanced to Liuhui; Helian Duo, out of strength and food, fled to the Tuyuhun and then to Youzhou; Yunzhou was pacified.
value.literal: In the seventh month Wuhuang advanced to Liuhui; Helian Duo, strength exhausted and provisions spent, fled to the Tuyuhun, then went to You Prefecture; Yun Prefecture was pacified.

value.zh: 武皇表石善友為大同軍防禦使。
value.en: Wuhuang memorialized that Shi Shanyou be made defense commissioner of the Datong Army.
value.literal: Wuhuang memorialized that Shi Shanyou be made defense commissioner of the Datong Army.

value.zh: 邢州節度使李存孝以鎮州王熔托附汴人，謀亂河朔，北連燕寇，請乘雲、代之捷，平定燕、趙，武皇然之。
value.en: Li Cunxiao of Xing, seeing that Wang Rong of Zhen had thrown in with Bian, plotted to stir trouble in Hebei and ally with Yan in the north; he asked to use the Yun and Dai victories to pacify Yan and Zhao, and Wuhuang agreed.
value.literal: Xing military commissioner Li Cunxiao, because Zhen's Wang Rong had entrusted himself to Bian, plotted to throw Hebei into disorder and link with northern Yan raiders; he asked to use the victory at Yun and Dai to pacify Yan and Zhao; Wuhuang agreed.

value.zh: 八月，大搜於晉陽，遂南巡澤、潞，略地懷、孟，河陽趙克裕望風送款，請修鄰好。
value.en: In the eighth month he held a great hunt at Jinyang, then marched south through Ze and Lu and overran Huai and Meng; Zhao Keyu of Heyang submitted at his approach and asked for peace between neighbors.
value.literal: In the eighth month a great hunt was held at Jinyang; then he toured south through Ze and Lu, overran the lands of Huai and Meng; Heyang's Zhao Keyu submitted at the first rumor of his approach and asked for neighborly peace.

value.zh: 九月，蒐於邢州。
value.en: In the ninth month he hunted at Xingzhou.
value.literal: In the ninth month a hunt at Xing Prefecture.

value.zh: 十月，李存孝董前軍攻臨城，鎮人五萬營於臨城西北龍尾崗。
value.en: In the tenth month Li Cunxiao led the vanguard against Lincheng; fifty thousand men of Zhen camped on Longwei Ridge northwest of the city.
value.literal: In the tenth month Li Cunxiao directed the vanguard to attack Lincheng; fifty thousand Zhen troops encamped at Longwei Ridge northwest of Lincheng.

value.zh: 武皇令李存審、李存賢以步軍攻之，鎮人大敗，殺獲萬計，拔臨城，進攻元氏。
value.en: Wuhuang sent Li Cunshen and Li Cunxian with infantry against them; the Zhen army was routed, with tens of thousands killed or taken; Lincheng fell and the attack moved on Yuanshi.
value.literal: Wuhuang ordered Li Cunshen and Li Cunxian with foot troops to attack them; the Zhen army was badly defeated, with tens of thousands killed or captured; Lincheng was taken and the attack pressed on Yuanshi.

value.zh: 幽州李匡威以步騎五萬營於鄗邑，以援鎮州，武皇分兵大掠，旋軍邢州。
value.en: Li Kuangwei of Youzhou camped at Hao with fifty thousand foot and horse to relieve Zhen; Wuhuang split his forces for wide raiding and then wheeled back to Xingzhou.
value.literal: Youzhou's Li Kuangwei with fifty thousand foot and horse encamped at Hao town to relieve Zhen; Wuhuang divided his forces for wide plunder and then turned the army back to Xing.

value.zh: 八月，赫連鐸誘幽州李匡威之眾八萬，寇天成軍，遂攻雲州，營於州北，連亙數里。
value.en: In the eighth month Helian Duo won over eighty thousand of Li Kuangwei's Youzhou troops, struck Tiancheng Army, then besieged Yunzhou with camps stretching several li north of the city.
value.literal: Eighth month, Helian Duo induced eighty thousand of Youzhou Li Kuangwei's troops, raided Tiancheng Army, then attacked Yunzhou, encamping north of the prefecture in a line several li long.

value.zh: 武皇潛軍入於雲州，詰旦，出騎軍以擊之，斬獲數萬，李匡威燒營而遁。
value.en: Wuhuang slipped into Yunzhou with his army; at dawn his horsemen fell on them, killing or capturing tens of thousands, and Li Kuangwei burned his camp and fled.
value.literal: Wuhuang secretly entered Yunzhou with troops; at dawn he led cavalry out to attack, beheading and capturing tens of thousands; Li Kuangwei burned his camp and fled.

value.zh: 十月，邢州李存孝叛，納款於梁，李存信構之也。
value.en: In the tenth month Li Cunxiao of Xingzhou rebelled and went over to Liang after Li Cunxin set him up.
value.literal: Tenth month, Xingzhou's Li Cunxiao rebelled, submitted allegiance to Liang; Li Cunxin had framed him.

value.zh: 八月壬戌，天子自華還宮。
value.en: On renxu in the eighth month the emperor returned from Hua to the capital.
value.literal: On renxu of the eighth month the Son of Heaven returned from Hua to the palace.

value.zh: 是時，車駕初復，而欲諸侯輯睦，賜武皇詔，令與汴帥通好。
value.en: The court had only just returned to Chang'an and wanted peace among the warlords; Wuhuang was ordered to reconcile with the Bian commander.
value.literal: At that time the carriage had just returned and the court wished the feudatories to live in harmony; an edict was granted to Wuhuang to make peace with the Bian commander.

value.zh: 武皇不欲先下汴帥，乃致書於鎮州王鎔，令導其意。
value.en: Unwilling to make the first move toward Bian, Wuhuang wrote Wang Rong of Zhenzhou to sound him out.
value.literal: Wuhuang did not wish to yield first to the Bian commander; he wrote to Wang Rong of Zhen prefecture to convey his intent.

value.zh: 明年，汴帥遣使奉書幣來修好，武皇亦報之。
value.en: The following year the Bian commander sent envoys with letters and gifts to reopen relations, and Wuhuang answered in kind.
value.literal: The next year the Bian commander sent envoys with letters and gifts to restore good relations; Wuhuang also replied.

value.zh: 自是使車交馳，朝野相賀。
value.en: Envoys then traveled constantly between the two sides, and the realm breathed easier.
value.literal: From then envoys shuttled back and forth, and court and countryside rejoiced.

value.zh: 九月，武皇遣周德威、李嗣昭率兵三萬出青山口，以迫邢、洺。
value.en: In the ninth month Wuhuang sent Zhou Dewei and Li Sizhao with thirty thousand men through Qing Mountain Pass against Xing and Ming.
value.literal: Ninth month, Wuhuang sent Zhou Dewei and Li Sizhao with thirty thousand men out Qing Mountain Pass to press Xing and Ming.

value.zh: 十月，遇汴將葛從周於張公橋，既戰，我軍大敗。
value.en: In the tenth month they met Ge Congzhou at Zhanggong Bridge and were routed.
value.literal: Tenth month, they met the Bian general Ge Congzhou at Zhanggong Bridge; after battle our army was utterly defeated.

value.zh: 是月，河中王珂來告急，言王珙引汴軍來寇，武皇遣李嗣昭將兵三千以援之，屯於胡壁堡。
value.en: That month Wang Ke of Hezhong begged for help against Wang Gong and the Bian army; Wuhuang sent Li Sizhao with three thousand men to Hubi Fort.
value.literal: That month Wang Ke of Hezhong reported urgency, saying Wang Gong was leading the Bian army to raid; Wuhuang sent Li Sizhao with three thousand men to aid him, encamped at Hubi Fort.

value.zh: 汴軍萬餘人來拒戰，嗣昭擊退之。
value.en: When more than ten thousand Bian troops came up, Sizhao beat them back.
value.literal: More than ten thousand Bian troops came to resist; Sizhao repelled them.

value.zh: 景福元年正月，鎮州王鎔恃燕人之援，率兵十餘萬攻邢州之堯山。
value.en: In the first month of Jingfu 1, Wang Rong of Zhenzhou, backed by the Yan, marched more than one hundred thousand men against Yaoshan in Xingzhou.
value.literal: First month of Jingfu 1, Wang Rong of Zhenzhou, relying on Yan aid, led more than one hundred thousand men to attack Yaoshan in Xingzhou.

value.zh: 武皇遣李存信將兵應援，李存孝素與存信不協，遞相猜貳，留兵不進。
value.en: Wuhuang sent Li Cunxin to relieve the siege, but Li Cunxiao, long at odds with Cunxin, each suspecting the other, kept his troops from advancing.
value.literal: Wuhuang sent Li Cunxin with troops to relieve the siege; Li Cunxiao had long been at odds with Cunxin, each suspecting the other, and held his men back.

value.zh: 武皇又遣李嗣勳、李存審將兵援之，大破燕、趙之眾，斬首三萬，收其軍實。
value.en: Wuhuang then sent Li Sixun and Li Cunshen to reinforce them, routed the Yan and Zhao armies, took thirty thousand heads, and captured their stores.
value.literal: Wuhuang also sent Li Sixin and Li Cunshen with troops to reinforce them, thoroughly defeated the Yan and Zhao forces, beheaded thirty thousand, and seized their military stores.

value.zh: 三月，武皇進軍渡滹沱，攻欒城，下鼓城、槁城。
value.en: In the third month he advanced across the Hutuo, attacked Luancheng, and took Gucheng and Gaocheng.
value.literal: Third month, Wuhuang advanced, crossed the Hutuo, attacked Luancheng, and took Gucheng and Gaocheng.

value.zh: 四月，燕軍寇雲、代，武皇班師。
value.en: In the fourth month Yan forces raided Yun and Dai, and Wuhuang withdrew.
value.literal: Fourth month, Yan troops raided Yun and Dai; Wuhuang withdrew the army.

value.zh: 王弘，字休元，琅邪临沂人也。
value.en: Wang Hong, courtesy name Xiuyuan, came from Langya commandery, Linyi county.
value.literal: Wang Hong, styled Xiuyuan, was a man of Langya Linyi.

value.zh: 曾祖导，晋丞相，祖洽，中领军，父珣，司徒。
value.en: His great-grandfather Dao had served as Chancellor of Jin; his grandfather Qia as Central Army Commander; his father Xun as Minister of Education.
value.literal: His great-grandfather Dao was Chancellor of Jin; his grandfather Qia was Central Army Commander; his father Xun was Minister of Education.

value.zh: 論曰：語云：「不有君子，其能國乎？」。
value.en: Commentary: The saying runs: "Without gentlemen, how can there be a state?"
value.literal: Commentary says: The saying goes: "Without gentlemen, how can there be a state?"

value.zh: 晉自中原沸騰，介居江左，以一隅之地，抗衡上國，年移三百，蓋有憑焉。
value.en: From the time Jin's heartland boiled and they held east of the river, one corner balancing the northern empire for three hundred years—they surely had something to lean on.
value.literal: From the time Jin's central plains seethed and they dwelt east of the river, with one corner of land balancing the upper state, years moved three hundred—surely there was reliance.

value.zh: 其初諺云：「王與馬，共天下。」
value.en: An early proverb said: "The Wangs and the Mas share the realm."
value.literal: At the beginning the proverb said: "Wang and Ma share all under heaven together."

value.zh: 蓋王氏人倫之盛，實始是矣。
value.en: The Wang clan's eminence among men truly began here.
value.literal: Truly the Wang clan's human excellence began here.

value.zh: 及夫休元弟兄，並舉棟樑之任，下逮世嗣，無虧文雅之風。
value.en: When Xiuyuan and his brothers together bore the weight of state, down through later heirs the refined literary tradition did not fail.
value.literal: When Xiuyuan and his brothers together bore pillar-and-beam responsibility, down to later heirs, the refined literary wind was not lost.

value.zh: 其所以簪纓不替，豈徒然也。
value.en: That their line held rank without break—was it mere chance?
value.literal: That their official caps were not replaced—was it for nothing?

value.zh: 僧達倡狂成性，元長躁競不止。
value.en: Sengda was wild arrogance incarnate; Yuanchang's restless ambition never ceased.
value.literal: Sengda's wild arrogance was his nature; Yuanchang's restless striving never ceased.

value.zh: 戴法興 徐爰 阮佃夫 紀僧真 劉系宗 茹法亮 呂文顯 茹法珍 周石珍 陸驗 司馬申 施文慶 沈客卿 孔範
value.en: Dai Faxing, Xu Ai, Ruan Dianfu, Ji Sengzhen, Liu Xizong, Ru Faliang, Lü Wenxian, Ru Fazhen, Zhou Shizhen, Lu Yan, Sima Shen, Shi Wenqing, Shen Keqing, and Kong Fan
value.literal: Dai Faxing, Xu Ai, Ruan Dianfu, Ji Sengzhen, Liu Xizong, Ru Faliang, Lü Wenxian, Ru Fazhen, Zhou Shizhen, Lu Yan, Sima Shen, Shi Wenqing, Shen Keqing, and Kong Fan

value.zh: 系宗久在朝省，閑於職事，武帝常云：「學士輩不堪經國，唯大讀書耳。
value.en: Xizong had long served in court offices and was adept at administrative work. Emperor Wu often said, "These scholar-officials cannot govern the state—they merely read books at great length.
value.literal: Xizong had long served in court offices and was adept at administrative affairs. Emperor Wu often said, "These scholar-officials cannot manage the state—they merely read books extensively.

value.zh: 經國，一劉系宗足矣。
value.en: For governing the state, one Liu Xizong is enough.
value.literal: For governing the state, one Liu Xizong is enough.

value.zh: 沈約、王融數百人，于事何用。」
value.en: Of what use are Shen Yue, Wang Rong, and their hundreds for practical affairs?"
value.literal: Of what use are Shen Yue, Wang Rong, and their hundreds for practical matters?"

value.zh: 其重吏事如此。
value.en: Such was the weight he placed on practical administration.
value.literal: Such was the weight he placed on practical administration.

value.zh: 建武二年，卒官。
value.en: In the second year of Jianwu he died in office.
value.literal: In the second year of Jianwu he died in office.

value.zh: 時有綦母珍之，居舍人之任，凡所論薦，事無不允。
value.en: At this time Qimu Zhenzhi held the post of attendant, and whatever nominations he put forward were invariably approved.
value.literal: At this time there was Qimu Zhenzhi, who held the post of attendant; whatever nominations he put forward were invariably approved.

value.zh: 內外要職及郡丞尉，皆論價而後施行。
value.en: Important posts inside and outside the court, as well as county assistant magistrates and commandants, were all sold by negotiated price before appointment.
value.literal: Important posts inside and outside the court, as well as county assistant magistrates and commandants, all were sold by negotiated price before appointment.

value.zh: 貨賄交至，旬月之間，累至千金。
value.en: Bribes poured in without cease, and within a month or so they accumulated to a thousand gold pieces.
value.literal: Bribes flowed in without cease; within a month or so they accumulated to a thousand gold pieces.

value.zh: 帝給珍之宅，宅邊又有空宅，從即並取，輒令材官營作，不關詔旨。
value.en: The emperor granted Zhenzhi a residence. There was another empty residence beside it, which he seized on the spot as well, then ordered the construction officer to build there without any imperial edict.
value.literal: The emperor granted Zhenzhi a residence; there was another empty residence beside it, which he took on the spot as well, then ordered the construction officer to build there without reference to an edict.

value.zh: 材官將軍細作丞相語云：「寧拒至尊敕，不可違舍人命。」
value.en: The construction officer general wittily echoed the prime minister's words: "Better to refuse the supreme sovereign's edict than to disobey an attendant's order."
value.literal: The construction officer general finely mimicked the prime minister's speech, saying, "Better to refuse the supreme sovereign's edict than to disobey an attendant's order."

value.zh: 珍之母隨弟欽之作暨陽令，欽之罷縣還，珍之迎母至湖熟，輒將青氅百人自隨，鼓角橫吹，都下富人追從者百數。
value.en: Zhenzhi's mother had accompanied his younger brother Qinzhi when the latter served as magistrate of Jiyang. When Qinzhi left office and returned, Zhenzhi went to meet his mother at Hushu with a hundred green-cloaked guards, drums, horns, and wind instruments playing, and scores of wealthy men of the capital followed in his train.
value.literal: Zhenzhi's mother followed his younger brother Qinzhi when the latter served as magistrate of Jiyang; when Qinzhi left office and returned, Zhenzhi went to meet his mother at Hushu, bringing with him a hundred green-cloaked guards, with drums, horns, and wind instruments playing; wealthy men of the capital followed in scores.

value.zh: 欽之自行佐作縣，還除廬陵王驃騎正將軍，又詐宣敕使欽之領青氅。
value.en: Qinzhi had himself served as assistant magistrate in the county. On his return he was appointed regular general under the Prince of Luling's fast cavalry headquarters, and Zhenzhi also falsely proclaimed an edict appointing Qinzhi to command the green-cloaked guards.
value.literal: Qinzhi had himself served as assistant magistrate in the county; on his return he was appointed Regular General under the Fast Cavalry headquarters of the Prince of Luling, and Zhenzhi also falsely proclaimed an edict appointing Qinzhi to command the green-cloaked guards.

value.zh: 珍之有一銅鏡，背有「三公」字，常語人云：「征祥如此，何患三公不至。」
value.en: Zhenzhi owned a bronze mirror with the characters "Three Dukes" on the back. He often told people, "With such an omen, why worry that the rank of Three Dukes will not come?"
value.literal: Zhenzhi had a bronze mirror with the characters "Three Dukes" on the back; he often told people, "With such an omen, why worry that the rank of Three Dukes will not come?"

value.zh: 乃就蔣王廟乞願得三公，封郡王。
value.en: He went to the Temple of Prince Jiang to pray that he might attain the Three Dukes and be enfeoffed as a commandery prince.
value.literal: He went to the Temple of Prince Jiang to pray for attainment of the Three Dukes and enfeoffment as a commandery prince.

value.zh: 啟帝求封，朝議未許。
value.en: He petitioned the emperor for enfeoffment, but the court deliberation did not approve.
value.literal: He petitioned the emperor for enfeoffment, but court deliberation did not approve.

value.zh: 又自陳曰：「珍之西州伏事，侍從入宮，契闊心膂，竭盡誠力。
value.en: He also declared in person, "Zhenzhi served humbly in the Western Province, followed the emperor into the palace, shared hardships heart and soul, and exhausted my loyalty and strength.
value.literal: He also declared in his own person, "Zhenzhi served humbly in the Western Province, followed into the palace, shared hardships heart and soul, and exhausted my loyalty and strength.

value.zh: 王融奸謀潛構，自非珍之翼衛扶持，事在不測。
value.en: Wang Rong secretly plotted treachery. Had it not been for Zhenzhi's protection and support, the outcome would have been unpredictable.
value.literal: Wang Rong secretly plotted treachery; had it not been for Zhenzhi's protection and support, the outcome would have been unpredictable.

value.zh: 今惜千戶侯，誰為官使者。」
value.en: If you begrudge me now a marquisate of a thousand households, who will serve as your agent at court?"
value.literal: Now if you begrudge me a marquisate of a thousand households, who will serve as your agent at court?"

value.zh: 又有牒自論於朝廷曰：「當世祖晏駕之時，內外紛擾，珍之手抱至尊，口行處分，忠誠契闊，人誰不知。
value.en: He also submitted a memorial arguing before the court, "When Emperor Shizu passed away, turmoil reigned within and without. Zhenzhi held the sovereign in his arms and issued orders by word of mouth—such loyal devotion in hardship is known to all.
value.literal: He also submitted a memorial arguing before the court, "At the time of Emperor Shizu's death, turmoil reigned within and without; Zhenzhi held the supreme sovereign in his arms and issued orders by word of mouth—such loyal devotion in hardship is known to all.

value.zh: 今希千戶侯，於分非過。」
value.en: To hope now for a marquisate of a thousand households would not exceed my due."
value.literal: To hope now for a marquisate of a thousand households would not exceed my due."

value.zh: 乃許三百戶。
value.en: Thereupon he was granted three hundred households.
value.literal: Thereupon he was granted three hundred households.

value.zh: 瞋恚形於言色，進為五百戶，又不肯受。
value.en: Anger showed in his speech and countenance. The grant was raised to five hundred households, yet he still refused to accept.
value.literal: Anger showed in his speech and countenance; the grant was raised to five hundred households, yet he still refused to accept.

value.zh: 明帝議誅之，乃許封汝南縣。
value.en: When Emperor Ming deliberated on executing him, the court finally granted him enfeoffment as count of Runan county.
value.literal: When Emperor Ming deliberated on executing him, he finally granted enfeoffment as Count of Runan county.

value.zh: 文苑四
value.en: Literary Grove, Part Four
value.literal: Literary Grove Four

value.zh: 及廣明之後，關東無復唐有，方鎮相侵伐者，猶以王室為名。
value.en: After the Guangming era the east of the passes no longer belonged to Tang; when circuit commissioners invaded one another they still took the royal house as their name.
value.literal: After the Guangming era the east of the passes no longer belonged to Tang; when circuit commissioners invaded one another they still took the royal house as their name.

value.zh: 及梁祖舉河南，劉仁恭輕戰而敗，羅氏內附，王鎔請盟，於時河北之事去矣。
value.en: When the Liang founder raised Henan, Liu Rengong was defeated for fighting lightly, the Luo clan submitted within, and Wang Rong requested alliance—then Hebei affairs were settled.
value.literal: When the Liang founder raised Henan, Liu Rengong was defeated for fighting lightly, the Luo clan submitted within, and Wang Rong requested alliance—then Hebei affairs were gone.

value.zh: 梁人一舉而代唐有國，諸侯莫能與之爭，其勢然也。
value.en: The Liang in one move replaced Tang and held the realm; the feudatories could not contend—the trend was thus.
value.literal: The Liang in one move replaced Tang and held the realm; the feudatories could not contend with them—the trend was thus.

value.zh: 向使以僖、昭之弱，乘巢、蔡之亂，而田承嗣守魏，王武俊、朱滔據燕、趙，強相均，地相屬，其勢宜莫敢先動，況非義舉乎？
value.en: Had Xizong and Zhaozong's weakness met Huang Chao and Cai Jing's turmoil, while Tian Chengsi held Wei and Wang Wujun and Zhu Tao held Yan and Zhao, strong and evenly matched—the trend should have been that none dared move first, how much less an unrighteous act?
value.literal: Had the weakness of Xizong and Zhaozong met the turmoil of Huang Chao and Cai Jing, while Tian Chengsi held Wei and Wang Wujun and Zhu Tao held Yan and Zhao, strong and evenly matched, territory connected—the trend should have been that none dared move first, how much less an unrighteous act?

value.zh: 如此雖梁祖之暴，不過取霸於一方耳，安能強禪天下？
value.en: Thus even the Liang founder's violence would have taken hegemony in one region only—how could he forcibly yield the realm by Zen?
value.literal: Thus even the Liang founder's violence would have taken hegemony in one region only—how could he forcibly yield the realm by Zen?

value.zh: 故唐之弱者，以河北之強也；
value.en: Thus Tang was weak because Hebei was strong;
value.literal: Thus Tang was weak because Hebei was strong;

value.zh: 唐之亡者，以河北之弱也。
value.en: Tang perished because Hebei was weak.
value.literal: Tang perished because Hebei was weak.

value.zh: 二王諸葛李孟
value.en: The Two Wangs, Zhu, Ge, Li, and Meng
value.literal: The Two Wangs, Zhu, Ge, Li, and Meng

value.zh: 始，全忠擊楊行密不能克，諷荊、襄、青、徐等道請己為都統以討行密，帝猗違未報；
value.en: Earlier Quanzhong had attacked Yang Xingmi without success and prompted the Jing, Xiang, Qing, Xu, and other circuits to ask that he be made overall commander against Xingmi. The emperor hesitated and gave no answer;
value.literal: At first Quanzhong attacked Yang Xingmi but could not overcome him; he prompted Jing, Xiang, Qing, Xu, and other circuits to request that he be made overall commander to attack Xingmi. The emperor hesitated and did not reply;

value.zh: 而珂與太原、鎮定等道亦請加行密都統，以討全忠。
value.en: while Ke together with Taiyuan, Zhen, Ding, and other circuits asked that Xingmi be made overall commander to attack Quanzhong.
value.literal: while Ke together with Taiyuan, Zhen, Ding, and other circuits also requested that Xingmi be made overall commander to attack Quanzhong.

value.zh: 繇是兩罷之，全忠怨珂，不忘也。
value.en: Both requests were denied. Quanzhong resented Ke and never forgot it.
value.literal: therefore both requests were set aside. Quanzhong resented Ke and did not forget it.

value.zh: 帝為劉季述所廢，珂憤見言色，屢陳討賊謀。
value.en: When Liu Jishu deposed the emperor, Ke's rage showed plainly in word and face, and he repeatedly urged plans to attack the rebels.
value.literal: When the emperor was deposed by Liu Jishu, Ke's anger showed in his words and expression; he repeatedly presented plans to attack the rebels.

value.zh: 既反正，首獻方物，帝甚倚之。
value.en: After the restoration he was the first to present tribute, and the emperor relied on him heavily.
value.literal: After the restoration he was first to present local products; the emperor relied on him greatly.

value.zh: 而全忠以克用方強，不敢加兵。
value.en: Quanzhong, however, dared not attack while Keyong was still strong.
value.literal: But Quanzhong, because Keyong was then strong, did not dare send troops against him.

value.zh: 及王镕詘服，拔定州，而克用兵折，乃謂其將張存敬曰：「珂恃太原侮慢我，爾持一繩縛之。」
value.en: When Wang Rong submitted and Ding Prefecture fell, and Keyong's armies were spent, he told his general Zhang Cunjing, "Ke leans on Taiyuan and insults me—take a rope and bind him."
value.literal: When Wang Rong submitted and Ding Prefecture was taken, and Keyong's military strength was broken, he then said to his general Zhang Cunjing, "Ke relies on Taiyuan and insults me—take a rope and bind him."

value.zh: 存敬以兵數萬度河，由含山襲，絳州刺史陶建釗、晉州刺史張漢瑜皆降，以何絪戍之，進攻珂。
value.en: Cunjing crossed the river with tens of thousands of men and struck through Hanshan. The governors of Jiang and Jin, Tao Jianzhao and Zhang Hanyu, both surrendered. He left He Yin to garrison the region and marched against Ke.
value.literal: Cunjing led tens of thousands of troops across the river, struck by way of Hanshan, and the governors of Jiang and Jin, Tao Jianzhao and Zhang Hanyu, both surrendered. He garrisoned the territory with He Yin and advanced to attack Ke.

value.zh: 全忠率師繼進，即劾珂交構克用，為方鎮生事，不可赦。
value.en: Quanzhong followed with his main army and immediately impeached Ke for colluding with Keyong and stirring trouble among the frontier commands—an offense that could not be pardoned.
value.literal: Quanzhong led his army in continued advance and at once impeached Ke for colluding with Keyong and stirring trouble among the frontier commands—unforgivable.

value.zh: 珂乞師太原，為絪所迮，不能進。
value.en: Ke begged Taiyuan for troops, but Yin blocked them and they could not get through.
value.literal: Ke begged troops from Taiyuan, but was hemmed in by Yin and they could not advance.

value.zh: 珂急使妻遺克用書曰：「賊攻我，朝夕見俘，乞食大梁矣。」
value.en: In desperation Ke sent his wife to Keyong with a letter: "The enemy presses me; I may be captured any day—I shall soon be begging bread in Daliang."
value.literal: Ke in urgency sent his wife with a letter to Keyong, saying, "The rebels attack me; any day I may be captured—I shall soon be begging food in Daliang."

value.zh: 克用答曰：「道且斷，往救必俱亡，不如歸朝廷。」
value.en: Keyong answered, "The roads will soon be cut. If I march to save you we shall both perish. Better submit to the court."
value.literal: Keyong replied, "The roads are about to be cut; if I go to rescue you we shall both perish. Better to submit to the court."

value.zh: 珂窮，遣使告李茂貞曰：「上初反正，詔藩鎮無相疑。
value.en: Cornered, Ke sent envoys to Li Maozhen: "When the emperor first restored order, he decreed that the frontier commands should not suspect one another.
value.literal: Ke, at his wits' end, sent envoys to tell Li Maozhen, "When His Majesty first restored the throne, he decreed that the frontier commands should not suspect one another.

value.zh: 而朱公不顧約，以攻弊邑。
value.en: Yet Lord Zhu has broken the pact and attacks my exhausted commandery.
value.literal: Yet Lord Zhu disregarded the pact and attacks my exhausted commandery.

value.zh: 弊邑亡，則邠、岐非君所保，天子神器斂手付人矣。
value.en: If my commandery falls, you cannot hold Bin and Qi, and the Son of Heaven's regalia will pass into another's hands.
value.literal: If my commandery falls, then Bin and Qi will not be yours to protect, and the Son of Heaven's sacred regalia will pass into another's hands with folded arms.

value.zh: 宜與華州韓公出精銳固潼關，以張兵勢。
value.en: You should join Lord Han of Huazhou in sending elite troops to hold Tong Pass and show military strength.
value.literal: You should join Lord Han of Huazhou in sending crack troops to secure Tong Pass and display military strength.

value.zh: 仆不武，公其惠我西偏地，以為扞守。
value.en: I am no fighter—grant me the western districts as a defensive hold.
value.literal: I am not martial—would you grant me the western districts as a defensive hold?

value.zh: 蒲，請公自有之。
value.en: As for Pu, I beg you to take it for yourself.
value.literal: As for Pu, I beg that you take it for yourself.

value.zh: 關西安危，國祚長短，系公此舉也。」
value.en: The fate of Guanxi—and the dynasty's future—rests on what you do now."
value.literal: The security of Guanxi hangs in the balance; the length of the dynasty's fortune depends on this move of yours."

value.zh: 茂貞不答。
value.en: Maozhen did not answer.
value.literal: Maozhen did not reply.
